page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-48 is an Arm-based general-purpose virtual machine configuration engineered for balanced computational workloads. Built on the 64-bit Arm architecture (arm64), this instance provisions 48 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 192 GB of system memory. The resource ratio stands at exactly 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, reflecting a standard general-purpose profile suitable for uniform resource consumption without memory or compute starvation.

The hardware configuration contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs or auxiliary hardware accelerators. Operating system partitions and application data rely entirely on external network-attached storage volumes. An architectural consideration of this platform is its Arm instruction set, which necessitates arm64-compatible binaries and container images rather than traditional x86 instructions.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated Arm core design delivers predictable core-level allocation and balanced multi-threaded performance. The n4a-standard-48 is oriented toward horizontally scaled container clusters, high-concurrency microservices, multi-stage build systems compiling for Arm, and medium-scale web application infrastructure requiring dedicated core isolation.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-48 is an Arm-based general-purpose instance designed for scalable multi-threaded server workloads. It delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs built on 64-bit Arm architecture and 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage solutions for operating systems and persistent data. Additionally, it contains no graphics processing units or hardware accelerators. By leveraging native Arm execution, the instance offers strong compute density and resource efficiency for standard enterprise deployments. Software stacks must support arm64 execution environments to operate effectively. Overall, the n4a-standard-48 is aligned with containerized applications, enterprise web serving tiers, automated build pipelines, and balanced microservices infrastructure requiring dedicated processor cores and predictable multi-threaded operational characteristics.
